text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 7.4% today after oil prices dropped sharply on news of renewed diplomatic efforts between Iran and Saudi Arabia to de-escalate regional tensions. For a refiner, lower oil prices are a mixed bag—crude costs less to buy, but the profit margin on turning crude into gasoline and diesel narrows when the price difference between input and output shrinks. The stock had already retreated over the past week as geopolitical risk premiums that had pushed crude to six-month highs began to unwind.

The timing matters: just days ago, tensions over Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure had driven Brent crude above $116 per barrel, which initially benefited refiners by widening their margins. Now that diplomatic signals suggest lower risk of broader supply disruption, that premium has evaporated—oil fell from the highs even as U.S. refinery utilization remains elevated at 93.4%, leaving less room for upside if margins compress further.
